newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gvts may need to approve Eurotunnel safety.
newsitem.headline: Gvts may need to approve Eurotunnel safety.

text.p: The French and British governments may have to step in directly to decide on reopening Eurotunnel SA /Plc's freight services if talks at the Inter-Governmental Commission (IGC) remain deadlocked, a source close to the negotiations said on Thursday.

The source said a last-minute hardening of position by the British delegation on the IGC, which oversees Channel Tunnel safety, had delayed a resumption of the freight Shuttle, which has been closed since a fire in the tunnel last November 18.
The IGC met on Wednesday and Thursday but did not allow a return to service, an IGC official said.
The IGC will meet again next week, the IGC official said.

"If the British have adopted a position totally incompatible with the French, it is possible the issue goes up to the governmental level," the source said, adding that the French parliamentary election campaign "does not help" the talks.
Eurotunnel had hoped to start test traffic from Thursday, building up to full service by mid-June, had the IGC given an early approval.

"But at the moment the British do not want to re-open heavy goods traffic in the original conditions. The Channel Tunnel Safety Authority's (CTSA) recommendations appear to be insufficient, or open to improvement," the source said. "There has been a real rethink since yesterday morning."

The expert panel CTSA, which reports to the IGC, published its report on Tuesday severely criticising Eurotunnel's procedures and called for a simplification, but did not call for a re-design of the controversial open lattice freight wagons.
Eurotunnel executives believe a closed wagon, demanded by the Kent Fire Brigade, would add too much weight and make the system uneconomic.
The CIG discussions hinge on the Shuttle design demanded by the British delegation, the source said.

British deputy prime minister John Prescott and head of the joint environment and transport ministry said on Tuesday that safety was of paramount interest in running the Tunnel and that he shared the concerns over the wagon design.
"The Inter Governmental Commission will be considering these points and I shall be instructing the UK's representatives to reflect my concerns," Prescott said on Tuesday.
The French election is due to be held in two rounds, on May 25 and June 1, raising uncertainty over who will be negotiating for the new administration.
